Rohas ne pehla route block kiya. Shreya ne uska planted foot padha, right se sharp cut liya aur use do steps peeche chhod diya.

“Rohas, nazar flag pe rakho. Ya attention kahin aur hai?” usne mudte hue kaha.

Rohas jawab banata reh gaya. Lokesh ne kuch nahi kaha. Woh Shreya ka pehla feint nahi, second pivot dekh raha tha.

Shreya flag ki taraf mudhi toh Lokesh apna outside foot pehle hi plant kar chuka tha. Narrow tag-lane mein dono ek saath aaye. Unki forearms takrayin; Shreya ne momentum sambhalne ko uske forearm par brief pressure diya. Lokesh ka haath clothed waist ke paas lage side training-tag tak gaya. Shoes chalk line par ghise. Shreya balance mein rahi—lekin Lokesh tag nikaal chuka tha.

“Ma'am, aapka second move predict ho gaya,” Lokesh ne seedha kaha.

Shreya ne uske haath ka tag dekha. Ek beat ke liye woh genuinely surprised thi, phir uski usual competitive expression laut aayi.

“Ek round jeetne se mujhe predict karna nahi seekh gaye tum.”

“Toh ek aur chance dijiye.”

“Next round.”

Meera ne short whistle maari. Kavita scoreboard ki taraf hansi. Rohas ne Lokesh ki foot placement dekhi; ab use samajh aaya ki woh first move par react kar raha tha, jabki Lokesh second move ke liye pehle se ready tha.

4:05 PM — WRAP

Shreya ne timer band kiya. “Bas. Flags aur tags rack mein. Recovery bhi training ka part hai.”

Meera ne paani peete hue shoulder stretch ki. Kavita ne forearm rotate ki aur joggers ki dusty seam brush ki. Rohas apna shoulder relax kar raha tha; Lokesh chalk se lagi palms saaf kar raha tha.

Shreya ne score sheet par Kavita ki first-round win aur Lokesh ka decisive tag mark kiya. “Dismissed.”

BEAT 12 — SAMAR & SHAAN: A SINGLE MEMORABLE INTERCEPTION

5:10 PM — SOCIETY COURTYARD

Car park karke Shreya ne belt kholkar seat par rakh di. Duty khatam ho chuki thi; khaki shirt ko trousers se untuck kiya aur neeche ka ek button khol diya, bas itna ki kapda kamar ke paas relaxed rahe. Collar ke top buttons ab bhi properly fastened the. Usne car lock ki aur bag kandhe par daal liya.

Courtyard mein New Year fitness activity ke liye resistance handle aur balance markers lag rahe the. Samar ek padded band ka tension check kar raha tha; Shaan side markers aur clear walking line dekh raha tha. Shreya ne unhe pehle pehchana—dono ke saath mahino ki gym practice aur subah ki bets abhi fresh thi.

Samar ne palatkar kaha, “Inspector madam! Aaj phir inspection? Gym ke baad bhi energy bachi hai?”

Shreya: “Tumhare markers dekhkar toh inspection zaroori lag rahi hai. Yeh line tedhi kyun hai?”

Shaan ne neeche marker seedha kiya. “Abhi test pending hai.”

Samar: “Subah tumne plank jeeta. Meri coffee appeal abhi bhi pending hai.”

Shreya: “Appeal ka form bhi submit nahi kiya, Mister Samar.”

Shaan: “Meri balance rematch bhi pending hai.”

Shreya ne bag bench par rakha. “Pehle equipment pass karo. Phir rematch ki baat hogi.”

5:17 PM — THE RESISTANCE TEST

Shreya ne khud partner-resistance check karne ko kaha. Samar saamne handle pakadkar position mein aaya. Shaan right side ka safety marker aur slack band dekh raha tha. Shaan ne floor ki edge ki taraf point karke bataya ki turning foot us line ke baahar nahi jaana chahiye.

Shreya ki smile pehle jaisi thi. Anaya ke janam ke baad uska figure pehle se fuller aur mature hua tha; khaki shirt shoulders ke neeche zyada fitted baithti thi, jabki untucked kamar ke paas halka loose fall de rahi thi. Regular workouts ne uske legs aur core ko mazboot banaya tha. Samar aur Shaan ke saamne woh kisi nayi student ki tarah nahi, purani competitor ki tarah khadi thi.

“Ready?” Samar ne poocha.

“Tum ho toh try kar leti hoon,” Shreya ne jawab diya. “Is baar count mat khona.”

Samar ne band ko resistance diya. Shreya ne pehla step control mein liya, doosra bhi. Teesre count par usne direction change ki, lekin band ki tension Samar ki step adjustment se ekdam kam hui. Shreya ka weight ek pace sideways gaya—right shoe ki edge marker par aa gayi. Girne se pehle hi dono bhai move kar chuke the.

5:19 PM. Band tension kam hote hi Shreya ka weight right marker ki taraf gaya. Samar front-left se aaya, palm uski upper back / shoulder blade ke neeche secure support diya aur doosre forearm se outer upper arm steady kiya. Shaan right side se loose band kheench raha tha; uska doosra haath Shreya ki clothed side-waist ko firmly guide karke marker se clear kiya. Dono supports ek hi 2–3 second weight-shift mein simultaneous the. Shreya ne turant pair jamaye aur apna weight sambhala. Dono supports turant release hue; na koi extra hold hua, na doosra accident.

“Ah—” Shreya ki saans se ek chhota sa startled sound nikla. Uski ungliyan ek pal Samar ke forearm ke against tanni, phir usne dono pair jamaye. Samaanya drill mein woh aise support ki aadat rakhti thi; lekin Vivek ki subah wali kiss abhi uske zehan mein thi, isliye us pal ki nazdeeki use expected se zyada noticeable lagi. Uska dil ek beat tez hua. Usne seedhi hokar dono se distance apne aap bana liya.

Samar ne handle dekha, phir uski taraf. Uski teasing ek second ko ruki. “Theek ho?”

“Main theek hoon,” Shreya ne kaha. “Tumhara third count galat tha.”

Shaan ne marker check kiya. “Band slack hua, foot edge par aaya. Ab line theek karta hoon.”

Samar ne turant jawaab diya, “Ma'am ne mujhe pakad liya, ab form mein kiski galti likhogi?”

Shreya ne eyebrow uthayi. “Tumhara. Aur witness tumhara bhai hai.”

Shaan: “Witness ne dekha ki dono ko balance sikhna hai.”

Shreya hansi. Koi explanation speech nahi hui. Samar ka reflex khula aur fast tha; Shaan ka support measured aur quiet. Dono alag the. Shreya ne phir se belt-free loose shirt ko ek baar set kiya aur saamne dekha—ab uske chehre par competitive smile laut aayi thi.

5:25 PM — THE AFTER-EFFECT

Samar handle ki tension dobara check karne laga; Shaan ne marker straight kar diya. Shreya ki saans ab normal thi, phir bhi upper back aur side-waist par dono supports ka alag-alag pressure kuch seconds tak yaad raha. Woh discomfort nahi tha, bas ek naya, unexpected awareness. Usne baat ko wahi khatam kiya, extra practice aur second accident ka bahaana nahi banaya.

Shreya: “Samar—energy zyada, control thoda kam.”

Samar: “Aur Shaan?”

Shreya: “Control better. Attitude test hona baaki hai.”

Shaan: “Challenge aap choose karogi.”

“Bilkul,” Shreya ne bag uthaate hue kaha. “Aur tum dono yaad rakhna—Anaya ki mummy ko easy opponent samajhne ki galti mat karna.”

Samar hansa. “Coffee appeal ka verdict?”

“Reserved.”

Shaan: “Meri balance rematch?”

Shreya: “Kal gym mein milte hain. Dono ka score wahin decide hoga.”

5:33 PM

Samar band fold karne laga, Shaan markers sametne laga. Shreya ne ek chhoti smile ke saath security desk ki taraf kadam badhaye. Dono ne usse rokne ki koshish nahi ki. Aaj ka incident ek shared, unspoken training memory raha—pichhle bets ab bhi conditional the.

**Episode 03 · Scene 01 — The Presentation Nobody Heard**  
1 January 2026 · 1:40–2:10 PM · Conference Room, Gurgaon Arts & Science College

Shivani stood at the front of the room, college kurta neatly pressed, pallu pinned in place, laptop open on the table. The projector now showed clean academic slides. She clicked to the next one and began explaining the revised cultural-calendar proposal, voice clear and steady.

“Next week we have the inter-department rehearsal on Thursday. Attendance has already been shared with the class representatives. Any change in the main hall booking needs to be confirmed by tomorrow afternoon.”

From his seat on the left, Aarav watched her mouth form the words. The morning’s faculty-room line kept returning: *Attention earn karni padegi, Aarav.* He had smiled then. Now the same smile on the screen—wet hair, maroon blouse barely covering her, saree cloth clinging low on her hips—kept sliding over the present image of her formal kurta. He forced his eyes back to the slide.

*Subah tak main uske saath clever jokes kar raha tha. Ab uski private tasveer mere phone mein hai. Woh yahan bilkul normal khadi hai, aur mujhe pata hai usne woh photo kis confidence se li thi.*

His fingers tightened slightly on the pen. When she turned to point at the screen, the movement of her shoulder under the kurta made the remembered curve of her bare waist flash again. He looked down at his notebook and wrote a line he did not need.

Beside him, Principal Dheeraj sat straight, hands folded. Every few seconds his gaze slipped from the slides to the line of her neck, then corrected itself. The professional part of him kept repeating the same sentence: *I should have stopped it immediately.* The other part remembered how long the photograph had stayed on the screen before any of them moved.

*College mein itni composed rehti hain. Us photo mein bilkul alag thi. Relaxed. Wet. Smiling at someone who was not in this room.*

He cleared his throat once, unnecessarily. Shivani glanced toward him, assuming a question. He shook his head lightly and looked back at the slide. The contradiction sat heavy in his chest: the same man who was supposed to protect faculty privacy had the image stored on his phone. He shifted in the chair and made himself focus on the next bullet point.

On the right, Trustee Malhotra remained almost still. He had not spoken since the presentation began. His eyes moved slowly—face, hands, the way the kurta settled when she shifted weight. He was not comparing the present moment to the photograph as openly as the other two; he was simply holding both images at once and letting neither leave.

*Kitni carefully ready hui thi. Kisi ke liye. Ab yahan khadi hai, bilkul unaware ki teen log uski woh tasveer apne paas rakh chuke hain.*

When Shivani paused to drink water, Malhotra’s gaze stayed on the glass at her lips for a second longer than necessary. He looked away before anyone could notice, expression unchanged.

Shivani continued, unaware.

“The final list of participants will be locked after the rehearsal. I will share the updated sheet with all department heads by evening.”

Aarav’s pen stopped again. In his mind the formal sentence dissolved. He saw the same mouth that was speaking now, earlier smiling at the phone camera, water still on her skin. The thought stayed private. He did not let it reach his face.

Dheeraj checked his watch, then the slides, then her. The urge to look at his phone—just to confirm the image was still there—rose and was pushed down. He folded his hands tighter.

Malhotra listened to the numbers she was giving and filed them away. Underneath, the quiet fascination continued without urgency. He had already decided the photograph would stay with him. Watching her now only made the decision feel more settled.

The last slide appeared. Shivani closed the laptop.

“That covers the immediate schedule. If there are no further questions, we can end here.”

A short silence followed. Aarav gave a small nod. Dheeraj said, “Thank you, Shivani. Clear presentation.” Malhotra inclined his head once.

She gathered her papers, still believing the room had simply heard an ordinary academic update. The three men remained seated a moment longer, each carrying the same private photograph and three different versions of the same struggle to look normal.

The meeting ended at 2:10 PM. Shivani left first. None of them spoke about what had happened on the screen an hour earlier.

---

**Private fantasies (kept strictly internal, never spoken or acted on in this scene):**

- **Aarav** keeps returning to the idea of earning the attention she mentioned that morning—imagining what it would feel like if the woman who challenged him in the faculty room ever looked at him the way she looked at the phone in that photograph. The thought is charged and unfinished; he does not complete it while she is still in the room.
- **Dheeraj** fights a recurring image of the wet, relaxed Shivani from the photo standing in the same conference room, looking at him instead of the slides. Each time the image rises he forces it down with the reminder of his position. The conflict itself becomes the fantasy he cannot fully stop.
- **Malhotra** holds a quieter, slower picture: Shivani turning from the screen toward him with the same private smile, as if the photograph had been meant for him all along. He does not rush the thought. He simply keeps it, controlled and deliberate, while his face stays blank.

The presentation is over. She remains unaware. Continuity toward the 5:00 PM staffroom scene is open.

## Scene 03: Return to Gulmohar Heights
**1 January 2026 · 5:20–5:57 PM · College → Gulmohar Heights**

**FINAL PUBLISHED EDITION — AUTHOR APPROVED 17 NOV 2026.** Based on the five-beat Scene 03 plot with the author's five Grok corrections, preserving the separate future-night planning record.

### 5:20–5:45 PM — The ride back

Staffroom ka darwaaza band karte hi Shivani ko finally college ki shaam ki khamoshi mehsoos hui. Din bhar ke lectures, presentation aur rehearsal ki baatein uske dimaag mein ab bhi chal rahi thi. Laksh ke saath group-photo wala unexpected moment yaad aaya toh woh apni hi jaldbazi par halki si muskurayi. *Aaj ek normal photo lena bhi project ban gaya.*

Woh seedhiyan utar kar parking mein aayi. Deep-plum kurta aur ivory dupatta wahi the jo usne college ke liye pehne the. Usne dupatta sambhala, bag scooty par rakha aur helmet pehen liya. Na outfit change hua, na koi naya campus encounter. Staffroom ki photo Arjun ko group mein bhejni thi; Shivani ne phone check karne ke bajay scooty start ki.

Gurgaon ki shaam mein traffic dheere chal raha tha. Signals ke beech ek jagah rukte hue usse subah Rohan ka New Year surprise yaad aaya—ab tak uska answer nahi mila tha. *Ghar pahunch kar dekhungi. Pehle Tara aur Kavya ka haal poochhna hai.*

Use bilkul andaaza nahi tha ki college mein uski unsent private selfie ki copies kisi aur ke paas bhi hain.

Lagbhag 5:45 par Gulmohar Heights ka gate nazar aa gaya.

### 5:45–5:49 PM — Chairman ka inspection

Shivani ne society parking mein scooty stand par lagayi aur helmet utara. Bag shoulder par theek karte hi ek familiar awaaz aayi.

“Shivani ji!”

Mahendra Suri thodi door khade the. Haath mein children's programme ki printed proof sheet thi.

**Shivani:** “Namaste, Chairman sahab. Print mil gaya?”

**Mahendra:** “Mil toh gaya. Lekin aapki final nazar ke bina kaise bhej doon?”

Shivani ne paper ki taraf haath badhaya. Mahendra ne sheet di. Jab Shivani haath badha kar paper leti hai toh deep-plum kurta uski waist par tight hota hai. Back se fabric thoda stretch hota hai, dupatta ek side se slip karta hai. Mahendra ki nazar usi jagah ruk jaati hai—kurte ki fitting front se cleavage line tak, peeche se waist curve tak. Woh sheet de chuka hota hai lekin aankhein abhi bhi uske mudne par hain. Shivani page par event date dekh rahi thi; jab usne sir uthaya toh Mahendra ne kaam ke bajay us par comment kiya.

**Mahendra:** “Shivani ji, aaj aapki kurti ki fitting front aur back dono taraf se kaafi attention kheench rahi hai. Chairman ka concentration bhi test ho raha hai.”

Shivani ne sheet neeche ki. Uski ek eyebrow halki uthi.

**Shivani:** **“Chairman sahab, aapka inspection society ka hai ya mera? Aapki nazar kuch zyada personal ho rahi hai.”**

Mahendra ek second chup rehta hai. Uske dimaag mein abhi bhi woh image hai—kurta waist par tight, back se fabric stretch, dupatta slip hota hua. Woh hasne ki koshish karta hai lekin aawaz thodi heavy aati hai. *Chairman hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki aankhein band kar loon.*

Mahendra ek lamhe ke liye apna next sentence bhool gaye. Woh muskura kar baat halka karne lage.

**Mahendra:** “Aap toh meri har baat pakad leti hain.”

**Shivani:** **“Phir sambhal kar bola kijiye. Children's programme ka print dikhaaiye.”**

Usne ungli se sheet par ek line indicate ki.

**Shivani:** “Yahan juniors ke performance time aur registration desk ka slot overlap kar rahe hain. Isse correct karwana padega.”

Mahendra ne paper dobara dekha. Kaam ka issue genuine tha; personal remark ki jagah ab actual approval aa gaya tha.

**Mahendra:** “Haan, theek. Main boys ko bolta hoon.”

Shivani ne sheet unhe wapas di. Mahendra ko uske quick comeback ka asar ab bhi mehsoos ho raha tha. Woh conversation ko thoda aur kheenchna chahte the, lekin Shivani ne agenda clear kar diya tha.

### 5:49–5:51 PM — Familiar printwork duo

“Ma'am! Perfect timing!”

Ayaan ek folded display stand aur poster proofs lekar aa raha tha. Uske saath Armaan tha, haath mein corrected QR sample.

Shivani dono ko pehle se jaanti thi—society ke event posters aur print corrections ke kaam se. Ayaan aam taur par pehle bolta tha; Armaan proof ki chhoti galtiyaan pakadne mein tez tha. Inhe first-time strangers ki tarah introduce karne ki zaroorat nahi thi.

**Ayaan:** “Shivani ma'am, aaj finally proof approve karwa hi lete hain. Hum dono ki itni mehnat kuch toh deserve karti hai.”

**Shivani:** **“Pehle spelling aur QR scan pass karo. Compliments ka result uske baad.”**

**Armaan:** “Proof perfect hai, ma'am. Aapki inspection se bachne ke liye extra checking ki hai.”

**Shivani:** “Achha? Toh scan karke dekh lete hain.”

Usne apna phone nikala. Armaan ne QR sample saamne kiya. Link khul gaya, lekin children’s programme ke registration time par ek purana slot dikh raha tha.

**Shivani:** “Dekha? Perfect ka label thoda jaldi laga diya.”

**Ayaan:** “Humne poster perfect bola tha, form wale update ka credit kisi aur ko hai.”

**Shivani:** “Credit baad mein baantna. Pehle fix karo.”

Mahendra ne revised proof ki ek copy le li.

**Mahendra:** “Theek hai, main committee ke paas yeh rakh deta hoon. Aap log final kar lena.”

Woh parking ke doosre end ki taraf nikal gaye.

### 5:51–5:54 PM — The folding stand

Ayaan ne wall ke paas display stand khola, taaki Shivani poster ka actual size dekh sake. Armaan ek side se frame check kar raha tha.

**Ayaan:** “Yeh stand stage ke side mein rahega. Door se text readable hona chahiye.”

**Shivani:** “Bas neeche ka QR cut nahi hona chahiye.”

Woh thoda paas aayi aur sample ka lower corner seedha karne lagi.

Usi waqt stand ka ek folding leg poori tarah lock nahi hua. Frame halka sa ek taraf jhuka. Shivani ne reflex mein proof sheet bachane ke liye haath badhaya, aur uska balance shift ho gaya.

Armaan sabse kareeb tha. Stand jhukta hai toh Shivani ka balance shift hota hai. Armaan ka haath turant uski clothed waist ke side par aa jaata hai—fingers kurte ke upar se firm, body almost touching. Shivani ka haath uske shoulder par padta hai. Deep-plum kurta uski movement se aur tight hota hai, side se waist curve clear dikhta hai. Armaan ki saans rukti hai. Woh usse steady karta hai lekin haath jaldi nahi hatata. Ayaan poster pakad raha hai, lekin uski nazar bhi un dono par hai. Shivani ne bhi shoulder chhod diya aur seedhi ho gayi.

Ek second ka silence tha.

Shivani ne Armaan ko dekha. Woh aam taur par kam bolta tha; is baar react karne mein sabse tez wahi nikla.

**Shivani:** **“Armaan, stand pehle lock karo. Mujhe hi rehearsal prop mat bana dena.”**

**Armaan:** **“Sorry ma'am. Aap safe hain — stand ko ab doosra chance nahi dunga.”**

Ayaan ne poster ki edge seedhi karte hue dono ki taraf dekha.

**Ayaan:** **“Armaan, tum toh silently hero ban gaye. Main abhi bhi poster pakad raha hoon.”**

Ayaan poster fold karte hue sochta hai. *Armaan ne pakda, main dekh raha tha. Kurta peeche se kitna tight lag raha tha us second mein.* Woh kuch nahi bolta.

**Shivani:** “Aur poster pakadna bhi important hai. Warna heroism ke saath reprint ka bill bhi aata.”

Ayaan hans pada. Armaan ne jhuk kar stand ka locking pin check kiya aur is baar use properly secure kiya.

Armaan khada hota hai. Uske haath abhi bhi us kurte ka feel yaad kar rahe hain—waist par kitna tight tha, kitni der usne pakda tha. Woh Shivani ki taraf nahi dekhta, lekin dimaag mein woh second baar-baar ghoom raha hai. *Sirf support tha. Phir bhi…*

Shivani ke dimaag mein us pal ki sudden closeness reh gayi, lekin usne use drama nahi banaya. *Kam bolta hai, par zaroorat padne par fast react karta hai.* Agle hi pal uski nazar stand par thi.

**Shivani:** “Ab check karo. Agar ye programme ke din gira toh tum dono ko stage ke paas guard duty milegi.”

**Armaan:** “Ab nahi girega, ma'am.”

### 5:54–5:57 PM — Final proof, unfinished conversation

Stand ab stable tha. Shivani ne poster ek baar upar se neeche tak padha. Do changes bache the—registration time update aur performers ke naam mein ek spelling correction.

**Shivani:** “Yeh dono corrections Sharmi ko bhejo. Deepu se final display placement coordinate kar lena. Uske baad proof release.”

**Ayaan:** “Matlab ek aur review round milega?”

**Shivani:** “Kaam theek hua toh review round ki zaroorat nahi.”

**Armaan:** “Phir Ayaan disappointed ho jayega. Isse feedback lene ki aadat ho gayi hai.”

**Ayaan:** “Feedback se hi growth hoti hai.”

**Shivani:** “Toh aaj ki growth report: QR update, spelling correct, stand lock. Teen out of three complete karo.”

Usne approval ke liye relevant correction mark ki aur sheet Ayaan ko de di.

**Ayaan:** “Done, ma'am. Kal tak final version.”

**Shivani:** “Message kar dena. Ab mujhe Tara aur Kavya ko bhi dekhna hai.”

Shivani ne bag shoulder par set kiya aur Tower C ki taraf chal di.

**Armaan:** “Good evening, ma'am.”

**Shivani:** “Good evening. Aur stand ka dhyaan rakhna.”

Woh mudkar building ke foyer mein pahunch gayi. Peeche Ayaan aur Armaan poster fold kar rahe the; dono ki conversation ab bhi print corrections aur Shivani ke sharp comebacks ke beech chal rahi thi.

**Scene 03 ends — 5:57 PM. Shivani has not entered her flat.**

taniya.title: Senior Review — The Hidden Uncle Track

Mr. Mehra remote call par joined the review.

Pradeep: “Original bank trail aur journal check karo. Sirf final balance ka screenshot enough nahi.”

Taniya: “Correction trace preserve ki hai. Original posting December 31 ki value date ko reflect karta hai; January 1 ka entry timestamp alag shown hai.”

Mr. Mehra (screen): “Supporting acknowledgment kisne authorize ki?”

Chirag: “Bank reference aur signed internal reconciliation dono attached hain, sir.”

Taniya: “Exception ko conceal nahi kiya. Do entries ka timeline mismatch highlight karke recommendation diya hai.”

**[T03-03-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]**

**Taniya conference table ke end pe khadi thi, sky-blue formal shirt uske torso pe fitted, charcoal trousers uski legs ko cleanly outline kar rahe the. Usne laptop se screen control karte hue controlled stance rakhi — shoulders straight, one hand lightly on the table edge. Colleagues ke sightlines se uska professional posture clear tha; koi extra exposure nahi, bas natural presentation movement.**

**[T03-03-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

Pradeep ne Taniya ko next slide kholne ko kaha. Chart par ek unexplained variance dikha.

Pradeep: “Is ₹2.4 lakh ko tumne material kyun nahi mark kiya?”

Taniya: “Absolute figure se nahi, account nature aur sampling threshold se decision liya. Is line ko separately flagged rakha hai, aur follow-up evidence pending hai.”

Vivek Suri: “Good. Pending ko resolved mat likhna. Confirmed aur provisional figures alag chahiye.”

Taniya: “Already done, sir. Revised report tab three mein hai.”

Vivek Suri outwardly professional raha. Taniya ki arguments ki clarity aur confident presence se woh impressed tha. Us attraction ko woh apne office behaviour se alag rakhta tha; Taniya ko uske private thoughts ka koi andaaza nahi tha.

**[T03-03-G02 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]**

**Vivek Suri head of table se Taniya ki confident presentation dekh raha tha. Uske sky-blue shirt aur charcoal trousers mein uski poised figure uske liye clearly attractive thi. Reader-only thought: woh privately imagine kar raha tha ki engagement se pehle ek consensual, private moment ho sake. Usne outwardly koi reaction nahi dikhaya — sirf professional nod. Taniya ko iska koi andaaza nahi tha. Yeh gym trainer Vivek Rao se alag character hai.**

**[T03-03-G02 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

11:59 AM. Andrea ne document control list par do signatures missing show kiye. Mehra ne kaha unka team faxed copy bhej sakta hai.

Andrea: “Scanned copy aaj mil jaye toh final packet time pe jayega.”

Mr. Mehra: “I can arrange it within an hour.”

Neha: “I will keep the document tracker live.”

Raghav ne Taniya ko next evidence tab ka number quietly bataya; usne bina interrupt kiye slide switch ki.

Pradeep: “Yeh workable hai. Lekin executive summary mein ek sentence add hoga—pending corroboration.”

Taniya: “Noted. Main draft thirty minutes mein revise kar dungi.”

Vivek Suri: “Final review evening se pehle close karna hai. Kisi ko forced approval nahi chahiye. Facts clean rakho.”

12:17 PM. Meeting khatam hone se pehle Vivek ne short schedule confirm kiya.

Vivek Suri: “Four-twenty par revised figures review rakhenge.”

Taniya: “Main confirmed figures aur exception register saath laungi.”

Pradeep: “Aur raw evidence kisi ko overwrite nahi karna.”

Chirag: “Version history safe hai.”

12:25 PM. Team room se bahar nikli. Raghav ne joke karna chaha, lekin Taniya already update notes dictate kar rahi thi.

Taniya: “Neha, signatures follow-up. Andrea, summary. Chirag, original trail. Raghav, updated binder index.”

Andrea: “Aur tum?”

Taniya: “Main evidence narrative rewrite karungi. Celebration ka slot baad mein.”

Work continued. Vivek Suri ki private admiration ek unspoken reader-only thread hi rahi; Taniya ke liye yeh normal senior audit review tha.

taniya.title: Office Chotu Punit Enters

12:25 PM. Taniya conference room se notes lekar nikli toh Punit records trolley ke saath corridor mein mil gaya. Uske paas labelled binders, fresh stationery aur delivery register tha.

12:39 PM. Punit ne table par old vendor ledger khola. Ek entry ke neeche handwritten correction thi.

Punit: “Yahan signer initials different hain. Isko exception list mein flag kar doon?”

Taniya: “Bilkul. Guess nahi karna kaun sa initial hai. Original scanned copy attach karo.”

**[T03-04-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]**

**Punit records trolley ke saath corridor mein khada tha. Taniya uske saamne sky-blue shirt aur charcoal trousers mein notes lekar nikli. Uske posture professional aur composed tha; Punit ne uski fitted office attire aur confident walk notice ki, lekin sirf reader-only shy admiration. Koi open reaction nahi.**

**[T03-04-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

Punit ko Taniya ki confident working style achhi lagti thi. Usne yeh baat kabhi kahi nahi; uske liye woh ek respected senior thi. Taniya ko bas uska quick attention aur improvement nazar aaya, kuch personal nahi.

12:55 PM. Neha aur Andrea ke beech half-hour handover hua. Chirag ne review checklist close ki; Raghav client attachment folder sync kar raha tha.

Andrea: “Punit, lunch kiya?”

Punit: “Abhi nahi. Register finish karke jaunga.”

Taniya: “Register lunch se zyada important nahi. Fifteen minutes le lo, phir baaki complete karna.”

Punit: “Thanks, ma'am.”

13:08 PM. Taniya ne next-day work allocation share kiya: archived entries verify, stationery stock check, scanned files align.

Taniya: “Aaj ke liye itna. Kal tumse full verification sheet chahiye.”

Punit: “Kal morning ready rahegi.”

13:15 PM. Punit register le kar apni desk par laut gaya. Raghav, Chirag, Neha aur Andrea ne lunch break plan kiya. Taniya ne laptop lock karte hue kaha:

Taniya: “Five minutes, then canteen. Reports bhookhe pet aur boring lagti hain.”
reviewNotes: Grok G01 illustrates Punit and Taniya standing in the corridor, although its insertion is after the 12:39 ledger check. This is a staging/time-position mismatch for author review; the source remains unchanged.

taniya.title: Lunch & Laughter

Taniya: “Good. At least ek useful New Year gift mil gaya.”

Neha: “Shaadi ke baad kya tum client data se bhi zyada strict hogi?”

Taniya: “Main abhi bhi strict hoon. Bas tumhare jokes ko exception de deti hoon.”

Andrea: “Exception toh dangerous word hai. Kisi ko extra benefit mil sakta hai.”

Chirag: “Aaj team mein sabse zyada benefit canteen wale ko mil raha hai.”

Raghav: “Us raat yaad hai? Chirag ne printer ko personal enemy declare kar diya tha.”

Chirag: “Printer jam hua tha, main nahi.”

Neha: “Aur Taniya ne sabko kaha tha, ‘panic karne ka time kal milega.’”

Taniya: “Haan, tabhi toh report time pe gayi.”

Sab hans pade. Is group ki intimacy friendship aur shared work-history ki thi; iske liye kisi artificial romantic introduction ki zaroorat nahi thi.

13:44 PM. Andrea ne phone camera on kiya.

Andrea: “Group photo! Audit zombies bhi smile karein.”

Chirag: “Raghav ki credit wali smile block karo.”

Raghav: “Main toh is photo ka lead actor hoon.”

Neha: “Lead accountant banne ki koshish kar lo pehle.”

Andrea ne Raghav ko sleeve se halka sa kheenchkar group mein side-by-side khada kiya. Neha ne funny paper-crown canteen receipt par draw karke Andrea ke haath mein thama diya. Taniya camera ke saath ek step peeche gayi.

**[T03-05-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]**

**Lunch area mein Taniya sky-blue shirt aur charcoal trousers mein baithi thi. Uske posture relaxed yet poised tha. Andrea photo lete waqt usne casually smile diya; fitted office attire naturally outline kar rahi thi without any extra exposure. Group chemistry light and collective.**

**[T03-05-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

Taniya: “Ek normal photo bhi mil sakti hai? Ya isko evidence exhibit banana padega?”

Andrea: “Normal photo kaise hoti hai, Mrs. Future Auditor?”

Chirag: “Wahi jisme tumhara hand movement blurred na ho.”

Raghav: “Everyone stand still. Main ready hoon.”

Taniya ne teen photos liye. First mein Raghav bol raha tha, second mein Neha aankhein band kar gayi, third finally usable nikli.

**[T03-05-G02 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

14:02 PM. Andrea ne group chat mein photo bheji, caption: “2026 audit survivors.” Taniya ke phone par Aditya ka ek message bhi blink hua: “Lunch kiya?” Usne short reply bheja—“Yes. Audit team rescued me from my own spreadsheet.”

Andrea: “Hamein toh abhi invitation design check karna hai.”

taniya.title: A Small Celebration — Andrea & Chirag
taniya.raw:
14:15 PM. Back at the audit section, revised report ki final cross-check shuru hui. Raghav subtotal verify kar raha tha, Chirag source ledger aur pivot output compare kar raha tha; Andrea aur Neha side-by-side exception worksheet pe thi.

Raghav: “I officially protest. Main bhi report pe tha.”

Neha: “Tumne report se zyada apna credit discuss kiya.”

Taniya: “Celebration over. Ab figures bhejo.”

taniya.title: The Second Flat — An Active Address

Taniya: “Lease agreement payment time par yaad aa jata hai.”

Raghav: “Client copy aur internal draft mein difference hai. Kaunsa final?”

Taniya: “Thank you. I'll circulate the final pack.”

Taniya: “You too, sir.”

taniya.title: The Last Office Hours

taniya.title: Guddu — The Wedding Quotation
taniya.raw:
20:08 PM. Cab Gulmohar Heights ke entrance par ruki. Taniya ne fare confirm kiya, laptop bag kandhe par dala aur security service desk ki taraf mud gayi. Reception ke paas event material ka register open tha. Guddu—society ka 23-year-old courier helper—wahan sealed handover packets sort kar raha tha. Woh Taniya ko pehle se jaanta tha; subah ke gym wala office trainee Punit usse bilkul alag person tha.

Guddu: “Happy New Year, Taniya madam. Wedding vendor ka packet aaya hai. Register mein aapka naam hai.”

Taniya: “Happy New Year. Aaj bhi delivery duty?”

Guddu: “New Year pe vendor log bhi busy hain. Shaadi ka season hai na.”

Guddu ne sealed quotation envelope uske saamne rakha. Taniya ne recipient aur vendor seal check ki, sign kiya, phir ek corner se papers count kiye.

Taniya: “Page one, page two... page four. Page three kahaan hai?”

Guddu: “Packet toh sealed hi tha, madam. Mere paas sirf dispatch slip hai.”

Taniya: “Shaadi ka quotation bhi incomplete? Guddu, tumhara delivery audit pass nahin hua.”

Guddu: “Madam, vendor ko bol deta hoon. Aapki shaadi mein bhi reconciliation pending hai!”

Taniya hans padi. Office ka mood abhi tak uske andar tha, lekin Guddu ki quick wit distinctly different thi.

**[T03-10-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]**

**Society entrance pe Taniya sky-blue shirt aur charcoal trousers mein Guddu se wedding quotation check kar rahi thi. Uske movement natural after commute. Guddu ka confident teasing reply; no personal affair. Outfit same, no exposure.**

**[T03-10-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

Taniya: “Chalo, tumhari entry provisional pass. Vendor se missing page kal morning mangwana.”

Guddu: “Ji. Waise aapko shaadi ka budget hi tough lag raha hai ya guest list bhi?”

Taniya: “Budget toh handle kar lungi. Guest list kisi aur department ka headache hai.”

Guddu: “Main delivery department se hoon. Mere paas sabhi ke complaints aate hain.”

Taniya: “Tab toh tumhara promotion risk management mein hona chahiye.”

20:12 PM. Guddu ne handover register ka photo system mein save kiya aur vendor ko follow-up message draft kiya. Taniya ne missing-page note envelope ke cover par likha.

Guddu: “Kal tak page mil gaya toh main aapko directly call kar doon?”

Taniya: “Call kar dena. But packet desk pe record karke hi dena. Audit ka first rule.”

Guddu: “Understood, madam. Aur congratulations advance mein.”

Taniya: “Thank you. Tum apni own New Year party kab karoge?”

Guddu: “Duty khatam hote hi, chai aur samosa se.”

20:15 PM. Taniya packet aur laptop bag lekar lobby ki taraf chali. Guddu wapas vendor counter par lag gaya. Is meeting se ek missing-document follow-up create hua; koi romance ya secret encounter nahi.

taniya.title: Karan & Aman — The Unexpected Lobby Collision
taniya.raw:
20:16 PM. Society foyer ke side passage mein folding programme boards rakhe ja rahe the. Karan aur Aman early evening event area se wapas aa chuke the; unka Shivani, Kavya aur Deepu ke saath wala encounter 19:23 par khatam ho chuka tha. Ab woh lightweight boards society storage tak pahuncha rahe the.

Taniya Guddu ke counter se aayi, ek haath mein vendor envelope aur doosre mein laptop bag ka strap. Narrow passage ke turn par Karan board lekar peeche muda. Ussi waqt Taniya ne corner cross kiya.

Karan: “Aman, woh stand—”

Board ka edge doorway ki taraf swing hua. Taniya aur Karan ekdum paas aa gaye; ek chhota accidental bump hua. Karan ka free hand ek startled instant ke liye Taniya ke charcoal trousers ke upar covered back-of-hip par laga, phir turant hat gaya. Balance lene ko Taniya ne Karan ki sleeve pakdi, ek second baad chhod di. Aman ne board ko stable kiya—uska Taniya se koi contact nahi hua.

**[T03-11-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]**

**Lobby mein Karan aur Aman se collision. Taniya sky-blue shirt aur charcoal trousers mein natural reaction. Light society banter; no heavy escalation. Outfit continuity, no new exposure.**

**[T03-11-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

Karan: “Sorry, Taniya! Board sambhalte hue tum dikh hi nahin rahi thi.”

Taniya: “Board apna sambhalo, Karan. Gym wali training lobby mein mat repeat karna.”

Aman: “Bhai, pehle rasta clear karna seekh lo, phir jokes.”

Karan ka usual playful comeback ek moment ke liye atak gaya. Taniya bhi briefly startled thi, phir apni firm voice mein wapas aayi.

[T03-11-G02 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]

**Karan ka haath turant hat gaya. Uske chehre pe clear embarrassment aa gaya — ears thode laal, nazar neeche, aur ek short, awkward breath. Taniya ek second ke liye startled hui, shoulders thode tight hue, phir usne apni sleeve se haath chhoda aur seedha posture le liya. Uske sky-blue shirt aur charcoal trousers mein balance quickly recover hua. Aman ne board steady karte hue dono ko dekha, practical concern ke saath — koi smile nahi, bas “sab theek?” wali nazar. Koi second touch nahi hua.**

[T03-11-G02 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]

20:19 PM. Aman ne board ko wall ke along place kiya.

Aman: “Tum theek ho? Envelope gira toh nahi?”

Taniya: “Haan, fine. Envelope important hai, lekin mere balance ka bhi insurance nahi hai.”

Karan: “Next time main traffic cone le aunga.”

Taniya: “Next time board lekar reverse karne se pehle rear-view mirror laga lena.”

Aman hansa. Karan ne ek hand-raised apology repeat ki; usse subah ka gym banter yaad tha, lekin is moment ko jaanbujhkar prolong nahi kiya.

Karan: “Okay, valid. Tum office se aa rahi ho?”

Taniya: “Haan. New Year gift mein nine-hour shift mili.”

Aman: “Hard day. Happy New Year, waise.”

Taniya: “Happy New Year. Ab tum dono boards correctly park karo.”

20:23 PM. Taniya lift ki taraf chali. Dono brothers event boards rakhne lage. Aman ne Karan ki taraf dekha.

Aman: “Next time passage clear karna.”

Karan: “I heard you first time.”

Taniya ne lift button press kiya. Kuch lamhon mein woh again normal mood mein thi. Karan aur Aman uske office interactions, second-flat subplot ya morning gym ke Soniya/Vivek details se anjaan the. Encounter yahin khatam hua, bina new romantic promise ke.

Grok G02 retells the startled reaction. This remains one accidental collision, not a second touch.

taniya.title: Soniya & Rahul — The Homecoming and the Unsaid Morning
taniya.place: Tower C · Soniya and Rahul's flat
taniya.raw:
20:28 PM. Tower C ke flat ka door khula. Soniya comfortable home clothes mein thi; dining table par dinner ki plates set kar rahi thi. Taniya laptop bag aur vendor quotation ka envelope lekar andar aayi.

Soniya: “New Year pe bhi itni late? Office ke paas wala flat convenient tha na?”

Taniya: “Tha, par ghar hi aana tha. Audit aur shaadi, dono ka overtime chal raha hai.”

Soniya: “Aur vendor ka packet?”

Taniya: “Missing page. Guddu ko kal morning follow-up diya hai. Marriage se pehle paperwork hi shaadi se zyada dramatic lag raha hai.”

Soniya: “Tumhara audit spirit shaadi ke din bhi leave nahi lega.”

Taniya ne shoes side mein rakhe. Soniya ne uske liye paani rakha. Din bhar ki noise ke baad ghar ka living room unusually quiet lag raha tha.

Taniya: “Didi, subah ki baat... tumne socha?”

Soniya ek pal ko ruki.

Soniya: “Haan. Aur main baat khud karungi. Tumse cover expect nahi karti.”

Taniya: “Good. Main bhi wahi chahti thi.”

**[T03-12-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]**

**Soniya aur Rahul ke homecoming. Taniya society flat mein sky-blue shirt aur charcoal trousers change karne se pehle. Morning conversation unfinished thread continue. Outfit same until change; no graphic.**

**[T03-12-G01 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]**

20:42 PM. Rahul office se laut aaya. Usne entry par shoes nikaale, Taniya ko wave kiya aur Soniya ke paas aaya. Dono spouses ne familiar affectionate hug share kiya; Rahul ne Soniya ke forehead par quick kiss diya.

Rahul: “Happy New Year, finally home. Tum dono ne dinner ke bina mere khilaaf meeting shuru toh nahi kar di?”

Taniya: “Jiju, aaj bhi meri audit duty chalu hai.”

Rahul: “Madam Auditor, aaj ghar mein bhi checking hogi kya?”

Taniya: “Aaj aap dono ka private review hai, Jiju. Main files rakhne jaa rahi hoon.”

[T03-12-G02 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION — START]

**Rahul ne Soniya ko familiar hug diya aur forehead pe ek short, soft kiss kiya. Soniya ne uske against halka sa lean kiya, shoulders relax hue. Taniya ne yeh dekha, ek soft playful smile diya, phir discreetly apna bag uthaya. Uske chehre pe koi heavy reaction nahi tha — bas ordinary sister-in-law ease. Soniya ne Taniya ki taraf ek brief, quiet look diya (morning gym thread abhi unsaid), phir Rahul ki taraf mud gayi. Koi extra intimate action nahi.**

[T03-12-G02 — GRAPHICAL DESCRIPTION WILL END HERE]

Soniya ne Taniya ki taraf dekha. Taniya ne koi signal pass nahi kiya; bas apna laptop bag lekar room ki taraf chali. Rahul ne apni jacket side par rakhi aur dining table par documents notice kiye.

Rahul: “Vendor ka kaam ho gaya?”

Soniya: “Partially. Kal Taniya check karegi. Aur... mujhe tumse ek aur baat karni hai.”

Rahul: “Kis baare mein?”

Soniya ke chehre par sharmindagi ka naatak nahi tha. Woh jaanti thi ki Rahul ko uski pehle ki limited-intimacy history pata hai; lekin aaj Vivek Rao ke saath jo hua, woh abhi share nahi kiya gaya tha. Rahul ko yeh naya event khud Soniya se sunna tha.

Soniya: “Rahul, subah gym mein Vivek ke saath ek baat hui thi. Mujhe tumse khud share karni hai.”

Rahul ne uski taraf poori attention se dekha. Detailed conversation abhi shuru bhi nahi hui thi.

21:00 PM. Scene yahin cut hota hai—Soniya ki choice to speak, Rahul ki response abhi unwritten, aur Taniya apne room mein. Episode 03 ka Taniya lane ghar laut kar is open conversation par end hota hai.
